84	## 4. Directness — the conditioning layer
85	
86	Directness conditions the weight a source carries for a given claim, as a categorical layer over the single ladder — never a separate hierarchy per scale, never a numeric confidence score (`evidence-methodology.md` §1.7; `schemas/directness.py`). Three dimensions: population-directness (EXACT/PARTIAL/PROXY/MISMATCH), value-directness (EXACT/WITHIN-TOLERANCE/NOT-FOUND/CONTRADICTED), scale-directness (DIRECT/ADJACENT/DOWN-WEIGHTED/NON-ANCHORING). They consolidate to one conditioning grade: DIRECT / DOWN-WEIGHTED / DISCOUNTED / NON-ANCHORING. The principle is **grain-matching, not specificity-ranking** — bidirectional per GRADE's directness (indirectness) domain: an aggregate systematic review is strongest for a population claim and down-weighted for a person-specific claim; a direct intervention study is the reverse.
87	
88	Four refinements close gaps found by adversarial review (2026-07-12); each is a separately ratifiable DR item:
89	
90	**G1 — Re-graining rule for T4/T5** `[NEW — DR-gated]`. `tier-system.md` §1 already says T4/T5 sources can support best-practice claims "if the standard itself rests on T1/T2 evidence." This document operationalizes that clause: a T4/T5 source is assigned `GRAIN_AGGREGATE` (and thereby escapes NON-ANCHORING at Population Mode) **only** when its evidence basis is documented as traceable to T1/T2 evidence, with that provenance recorded on the source record. Otherwise it keeps `GRAIN_CODE`. Untraceable standards convergence stays in the regulatory stratum where §2 put it.
91	
92	**G2 — NOT_ASSESSED is not EXACT** `[NEW — DR-gated]`. `consolidate()` currently treats a `None` population-directness as "not applicable — does not block," which is correct for claims where the dimension genuinely does not apply, but only 27 of 640 sources carry any `evidence_population_match` row — so at backfill scale, "never assessed" would silently grade as fully direct. The engine distinguishes **NOT_ASSESSED** (dimension applies, no assessment exists) from **not-applicable** (dimension genuinely inapplicable). A NOT_ASSESSED dimension caps consolidation at DOWN-WEIGHTED and flags the source for assessment. Absence of assessment is never treated as evidence of directness — the Altman & Bland distinction (`evidence-methodology.md` §2.4) applied to the project's own metadata.
93	
94	**G3 — Co-1 grain follows `co1_source_type`** `[NEW — DR-gated]`. Co-1 is not uniform in grain: `dpo_position_statement` is population-grain community knowledge (→ GRAIN_AGGREGATE); `lived_experience_publication`, `participatory_research` and individual-testimony corpora are individual-grain (→ GRAIN_SPECIFIC), which is also what `grain_for` gives any value it does not name. The column declares no CHECK; `schemas.enums.Co1SourceType` is its vocabulary (RULINGS R11). This makes the matrix row-pair in §3 mechanical, and it encodes the ethical rule already in `co1-operational.md`: a DPO position paper is community consensus — it anchors Population-Mode claims *and does not override an individual at Person Mode*; an individual narrative is the reverse.
95	
96	**G6 — Grain derives from (evidence_type × tier), not evidence_type alone** `[NEW — DR-gated]`. `standard_eb` spans two strata: T2 named-organisation evidence-based standards (synthesis-tier — the "same epistemic move as sr_meta, different machinery," `tier-system.md` §2) and T4 international standards (regulatory stratum). The current type-only default grains both as CODE, which would make T2 DPO/professional-body standards NON-ANCHORING at Population Mode — contradicting `evidence-methodology.md` §1.6, which lists Tier 2 among the anchoring strata. Resolution: `standard_eb` at T2 → GRAIN_AGGREGATE; `standard_eb` at T4/T5 → GRAIN_CODE (unless re-grained per G1). Grain assignment is a function of the (type, tier) pair.
97	
98	### 4.5 Genealogy — counting roots, not documents
99	
100	Directness conditions how much a source's *claim* weighs. Genealogy conditions how much a value's *apparent agreement* weighs. It gives the project's central adjudication — best practice versus consensus — a computable form. `[H1 — DR-2026-07-13-value-genealogy-and-derivation-handshake, ratified 2026-07-13]`
101	
102	The doctrine in one line: **precedent counts documents; evidence counts roots.** Twenty-four jurisdictions specifying the same figure is one fact about transmission, not twenty-four facts about disabled people. This is the §2 convergence-not-evidence rule pushed one level down — from *which stratum is agreeing?* to *how many independent measurements are they all agreeing about?* The corridor case is the worked proof (§8.1; `references/methodology/value-genealogy-worked-example-corridor-width.md`): 1500mm turning "circles" across 24 jurisdictions trace to a single 1970s anthropometric root whose own authors record it as needing updating; the 1800mm passing consensus has no traceable root anywhere in the corpus; 2440/2400mm has two independent roots (ASL proxemics, Co-1; swept-path anthropometry, T3) plus one untraced regulatory convergence.
103	
104	**Storage.** Each extracted value on `source_value_extractions` carries `root_id`, `root_type` (`measurement_primary` / `participatory_finding` / `committee_assertion` / `derived_calculation` / `untraced`), `root_ref_id`, `echo_of`, `measurement_paradigm`, `device_class`, `root_population_note`, `file_anchor`, `root_classification_basis`, `contested`. The discriminator is the view `v_value_independence`: independent roots **per parameter**, counting DISTINCT roots and excluding `committee_assertion`. *(Swept 2026-09-10 with migration 073, which names this file as a prose caller of that view. The sentence read "per (parameter, population)"; the population half went with migration 071, which took `population_code` out of the view's grain, and 073 re-derived the view a second time onto `parameter_id`. It groups by `parameter_id` alone — the lens is the determination's, not the root count's.)*

133	### 5.5 The derivation handshake — and the cultural-claim protection
134	
135	The corpus derives values along two paths that have never been required to meet: **top-down** from population and community (BPCs, Co-1, every population join) and **bottom-up** from function (the ICF-indexed `references/fdr/` corpus, deliberately population-blind at collection; the functional-deficit-auditor's population↔ICF mapping, which lived as unvalidated skill prose until migration 080 promoted it into the table now named `identity_icf_map` on 2026-09-13). 137	**The rule.** Every determination records `functional_basis` (mechanism type per the FDA taxonomy, ICF code(s), and supporting refs including FDR file anchors) and `derivation_paths` ∈ `dual` / `population_only` / `function_only`. Dual-path convergence is recorded as itself evidence — doctrine #3, convergence across independent axes, extended from evidence axes to derivation paths. A single-path assertion is permitted **only with a named-path rationale**, in the exact shape of the existing `single_axis` rule.

139	**The cultural/dignity-claim protection — a named commitment, ratified 2026-07-13.** Claims whose normative force is community-rooted remain **fully assertable as `population_only`**. The handshake makes a derivation *explicit*; it never requires a mechanism where the claim is cultural, and **no functional derivation may flatten, reduce, or override a community claim** — there is no bottom-up override of Co-1. A signing-space corridor width is not a wheelchair-envelope calculation that came out wrong; it is a different claim, held by the community whose language it serves, and it stands on that basis. This was ratified as a named commitment rather than inherited silently, because it is the dignity line the architecture exists to hold: it binds every register, every audience, and the engine. It is the determinations-layer expression of the asymmetry principle (§3, G4) and of G3's refusal to let population-grain speech stand in for individuals.

212	## 9. Academic rigour and ethics — the standing commitments
213	
214	**Rigour.** The architecture's methodological anchors, and where each is argued in full: correspondence to GRADE/JBI/SIGN and why wholesale GRADE adoption is insufficient for built-environment claims (`references/methodology-evidence-hierarchy-mapping.md` v2 — the directness layer *is* GRADE's indirectness domain, applied bidirectionally; synthesis-above-primary follows GRADE; the co-primacy of lived experience is a declared, argued departure, not an oversight); categorical rather than numeric conditioning (no false-precision scores, `schemas/directness.py` BOUNDARY note); determinism and reproducibility (pure determination function, `rule_version` + `derivation_sha`); falsifiability (every `stated`/`provisional` cell records what evidence would overturn it, `workplan/best-practices-assessment-system.md` §3 item 6); absence-of-evidence ≠ evidence-of-absence (Altman & Bland 1995, applied to cells in §2.4 and — via G2 — to the project's own assessment metadata); and the anti-hallucination gate (no determination without resolvable `governing_refs`).
215	
216	**Ethics.** The commitments are structural, not aspirational: CRPD Art. 4.3 grounds Co-1 co-primacy (Art. 9 ≈ Universal Mode floor; Art. 5 reasonable accommodation ≈ Person Mode; the full article-by-article critique is `governance/armature_v3_review.md`); epistemic justice is engineered — testimonial justice via Co-1's non-substitutable co-primacy and G3's refusal to let population-grain speech stand in for individuals, hermeneutical justice via the plain-language register receiving the *same* determination tuple as the technical one (I1: access to the same facts, not a simplified sub-truth); the carer is a distinct role, never a proxy for the disabled person (Art. 12 supported-not-substituted decision-making, `armature_v4.md` §4.5); representation-checking by disabled readers is an elevated-weight use-pattern whose failure overrides designer convenience (`audience-priority.md` §Within-primary); and the solo-authorship limit is declared on every Co-1-governed determination — pre-launch engagement with Co-1 is evidence-level, not participation-level, and CRPD Art. 4.3 is thereby honored in partial form only (`mission-and-epistemics.md` §Operational reality). Integrity here means the limits are rendered, not just recorded.
217	
218	## 10. What would falsify this architecture, and how it is checked
219	
220	**Mechanical checks (each must be shown firing on injected bad data before its pass counts):**
221	1. *Matrix–code consistency:* the sweep below regenerates §3's parenthesized outcomes from `schemas/directness.py` for all grain × scale combinations; any diff fails.
222	2. *Determinism:* the pilot engine run twice over the same evidence set yields byte-identical `derivation_sha` values.
223	3. *Invariants I1–I5:* over rendered output; unenforced (the check was deleted, plan step 1.6).
224	4. *State-machine integrity:* `scripts/validate_evidence_state.py` (governing_refs non-empty; `code_floor_only`/`regulatory_stratum_only` never `stated`; Tier-3-alone threshold).
225	
226	```python
227	# Matrix–code consistency sweep (§3). Run from repo root: python -c "…" or scripts/audit/matrix_consistency.py
228	from schemas.directness import (ALL_GRAINS, ALL_SCALES, scale_directness)
229	for grain in sorted(ALL_GRAINS):
230	    for scale in sorted(ALL_SCALES):
231	        print(f"{grain:>10} × {scale:<11} -> {scale_directness(grain, scale)}")
232	# Expected (must match §3's parentheses): aggregate×population DIRECT; aggregate×person DOWN-WEIGHTED;
233	# aggregate×universal ADJACENT; code×universal DIRECT; code×population NON-ANCHORING; code×person NON-ANCHORING;
234	# specific×person DIRECT; specific×population DIRECT (DOWN-WEIGHTED if generalizes_beyond_measured); specific×universal ADJACENT.
235	```
236	
237	**Falsification conditions (doctrinal):** this architecture is wrong if — a rendering pipeline honoring I1–I5 cannot serve a named audience's canonical use-pattern without breaching an invariant (audience needs and integrity actually conflict); or a real cell arises whose correct handling requires re-ranking the ladder per mode rather than conditioning it (D-D's core is false); or representation-checking by disabled readers returns systematic "this is wrong about my experience" verdicts on determinations the machinery marks sound (the machinery measures the wrong thing). Any of these routes to a DR, not a silent patch.

**RULE: "Axis" is descriptive vocabulary, not a domain identifier.**
The word is ordinary English for how something is arranged, and it must stay freely available for
that. **Precisely for that reason it may not name a specific vocabulary layer.** Overloading it costs
twice: the layer stops saying what it is, and the word stops being usable for plain description.

The layer currently called `axes` carries `icf_b_anchors` and `icf_d_anchors` — it holds
**ICF-anchored access needs**, and must be named for that. Pull a frame as **ICF codes with names**,
never as bare codes: a bare `axis_code` pull once framed four of five searches on `AX-AUD` alone and
hid that the slug also spanned `AX-SPR` (`sessions/session_2026-08-19-research-batch-01-room-acoustic-performance.md` §1(a)).

## Owner instruction 2026-11-15 — tasks of the remediation plan are stacked into a single pull request, not one pull request each

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "going forward, we will stack branches into single PR instead of one item per PR"

**Readings.** [ASSUMPTION: "branches" means the task branches the remediation plan assigns one to a task, and "single PR" means one pull request that carries several tasks as separate commits on one branch, so a task no longer waits for the previous task's pull request to merge — basis: the statement, given while pull request 235 was open on the working branch and T-006 was the next task]. [ASSUMPTION: each task still keeps its own commits, its own caller sweep, before-and-after check run, gate and adversarial pass, and its own entry in the pull request body; only the unit of merge changes — basis: the statement says nothing that loosens them, and the plan's tests are what make a stacked pull request reviewable].

**What it supersedes.** The sentences "One task, one pull request" (every task file, section 2 and section 11 step 5), "One pull request merges at a time" (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` section 2 item 2; the prior workplan's WR-1) and the "Do not start batch n until every READY task of batch n-1 is merged" of `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` section 1 item 2, as to the unit of merge only. Dependencies between tasks are unchanged: a task still follows the tasks it depends on, now as an earlier commit on the same branch, not a merged pull request.

**What it does not decide.** Whether CLAUDE.md rule 10 (tooling and research never share a pull request) is relaxed: it is not, and a stacked pull request carries tooling tasks only; a research task still goes in its own pull request. How large a stacked pull request may grow before the owner wants it split.

CONDITION: any session executing a task of the remediation plan, or asking whether a task waits for the previous pull request to merge.
ACTION: (1) Finish each task on the working branch (its own gate, adversarial pass and repairs, each a commit) before the next; open one pull request for the branch and add each task to its body; do not wait for a merge between tasks. (2) Keep tooling and research apart (rule 10). (3) The generated `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` is not edited by hand; its "merged" test reads merge commits and will count a stacked task as merged only when the pull request merges.
DATE: 2026-11-15 — owner instruction (typed words, quoted above).


---

## Owner instruction 2026-11-15 (later) — at the end of each batch, sweep the changes forward and backward and repair what was left, so nothing hangs

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "for unrepaired items: please sweep your changes at end of each batch both forward and backward to assess compatibility with existing work and proposed work, and then rectify accoridngly. we do not want to leave hanging unfixed work"

**Readings.** [ASSUMPTION: "unrepaired items" are the findings an adversarial pass raised and the executor reported without repairing, and every limit a task's own report states; "batch" is a batch of `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md`; "forward" is the proposed work (the task files of later tasks and batches that name anything the batch changed) and "backward" is existing work (the code, tests, skills, governance and derived files that already stood, and the earlier tasks of the same stack) — basis: the statement]. [ASSUMPTION: "rectify" means repair it in the batch's pull request where the repair is code or text within the executor's reach, and where it is a decision the owner holds (doctrine, taxonomy, a delegated resolution) put the question to the owner in the pull request and amend the affected task files so the question is not silently carried; a reported item is not an acceptable end state — basis: "we do not want to leave hanging unfixed work"].

**What it adds to the per-task process.** After the last task of a batch: (1) list every reported-and-not-repaired item of the batch; (2) read every task file of later work that names anything the batch changed and correct it; (3) re-run the checks of every earlier task of the stack against the final tree and re-grep the callers of everything changed; (4) regenerate derived files; (5) commit, push, and say in the pull request what was repaired and what is now the owner's question.

CONDITION: any session that has finished the last task of a batch of the remediation plan.
ACTION: run the sweep above before reporting the batch finished; do not report an item as "not repaired" without either repairing it in the sweep or naming the owner question and the task files amended for it.
DATE: 2026-11-15 — owner instruction (typed words, quoted above).

-- 107_drop_item_layer_cluster.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- the item layer is dropped from the schema (plan step 1.2; RULINGS R36).
--
-- THE OWNER'S REASON. The item layer was deleted from the database on 2026-09-01 because a
-- container named for its answer ("E-08 Corridor Clear Width (>=1200 mm Minimum on All Primary
-- Routes)") biases every finding filed into it (CLAUDE.md section 7; WRK-169, WRK-170). The
-- rows are gone; this removes the empty tables, the view and the foreign keys that still
-- pointed at them, so no writer can file into a container that no longer exists. WRK-170's
-- condition (the rows are archived) is met by _archived/data/corpus-pre-reset-2026-08-06.db and
-- the migration chain.
--
-- EVIDENCE (derived, 2026-10-14, before this migration; re-run rather than trust):
--   * every table below holds 0 rows:
--       select count(*) from <table>   -- each 0
--   * the only inbound foreign keys are from the tables below to `items`, and from `conflicts`
--     (also 0 rows) to `items`; `probe_population_links` points at `spec_value_probes`:
--       pragma foreign_key_list on every table
--   * the only view reading any of them is v_pmp_latest_walk (reads spec_value_probes); no trigger
--     reads any of them (sqlite_master).
--   * data migrations that write them:
--       grep -lE "(INSERT( OR [A-Z]+)? INTO|UPDATE|DELETE FROM) \"?<table>\"?[ (]" scripts/migrations/data_*.sql
--     finds only data_20260821185514 (jurisdictional_values) and data_20260901183203
--     (item_taxonomy_links). Both precede 095's AFTER_DATA marker (20260920060857), so the
--     runner replays them before this migration; no data migration after the marker names any
--     of these tables, so no marker is needed here.
--
-- WHAT IS DROPPED: items, item_audit_runs, item_bpc_links, item_taxonomy_links,
-- item_population_elaborations, term_item_links, room_items, case_study_specs,
-- economics_entry_specs, spec_value_probes, probe_population_links, jurisdictional_values, and
-- the view v_pmp_latest_walk.
--
-- WHAT IS REBUILT: `conflicts` (0 rows) keeps `item_code` as a plain column, without its
-- foreign key into `items`, by the 081 procedure (create the new table from the live DDL
-- changing only that line, copy, drop, rename, recreate the three indexes). The column and its
-- unique index stay: a writer still names an item code there, and dropping a column a writer
-- names is that writer's retirement, not this migration's (CLAUDE.md rule 5).

DROP VIEW v_pmp_latest_walk;
DROP TABLE probe_population_links;
DROP TABLE spec_value_probes;
----
-- 138_drop_medical_lens.sql
-- SCHEMA migration, GENERATED from sqlite_master of the schema-137 database. Owner instruction 2026-11-16, quoted in
-- references/project-standards.md ("Owner instruction 2026-11-16 -- the medical taxonomy, the medical maps and the
-- medical codes are deleted"): the medical lens is removed. Dropped: base_taxonomy_medical, identity_medical_map and
-- icf_medical_map (no row in any of them), and the medical_code column of gaps, specifications, search_executions, extraction_lens_links, determination_gates, source_value_extractions (NULL on every row of
-- every one of them). Tooling; no research row, no row changed or lost.
--
-- SQLite cannot drop a column that carries a foreign key, a CHECK or an index, so each of the six tables is rebuilt as
-- 114, 131 and 136 rebuilt theirs: the sequence floor of an AUTOINCREMENT table is captured (DROP TABLE takes its
-- row), every view that names a rebuilt or dropped table (and every view that names such a view) is dropped, each new
-- table is created, filled by column name, the old one dropped and the new one renamed, its indexes and trigger are
-- recreated, the floors are restored and the views are recreated from their stored text. The only edits to any stored
-- text are the medical-lens ones: the column, the term in the three CHECKs and the two unique indexes that carried it,
-- and the term in the six views that selected it. The foreign keys of other tables into a rebuilt table name it by
-- text and resolve to the new table.
CREATE TEMP TABLE _138_seq AS SELECT name, seq FROM sqlite_sequence;

## Owner statement 2026-11-14 (sixteenth set, last) — populations are still coded, through the ICF and access-need lenses

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "but ICF and access needs are supposed to be mapped to populations too so populations still get coded as a result"

**Readings.** [ASSUMPTION: a code value that carries an ICF code and an access need as its lens reaches the populations (identities) those codes map to; the identity is therefore coded by derivation through the existing mapping (`identity_icf_map`, derive the live rows with `select count(*) from identity_icf_map`), not written beside the ICF and access-need links; so OD-31 (a clause naming no group carries no identity of its own) stands, and the mounting-height and clearance defaults reach the wheelchair-user identity by the mapping from their ICF reach code and access need — basis: the statement, and rule 5 (point, do not copy)]. [ASSUMPTION: this settles the apparent clash between OD-31 and the worked defaults recorded by the integrator as conflict 25: there is no clash, since the identity follows the ICF and access-need links — basis: the statement]. [ASSUMPTION: the live mapping from access needs to identities was not found by name (`needs_code` has no `*_map` table among the tables listed by `sqlite_master`); whether it exists under another name, or the needs lens reaches populations only through the ICF mapping, is for T-126 to derive and report — basis: a search of `sqlite_master` for names with "map" or "lens"].

**What it does not decide.** Whether an identity named by the clause itself is written as a link (it is, as before); the coverage of `identity_icf_map` (61 rows today) for the ICF codes the defaults use.

CONDITION: any session assigning a lens to a code value, or reading the populations a code value serves.
ACTION: write the ICF and access-need lens in the recording call; reach the populations through the mapping; do not store the derived identity beside them.
DATE: 2026-11-14 — owner statement (typed words, quoted above).

---

## Correction and registration 2026-11-15 — the lens of a code value is judged and written at recording; the maps propose; OD-67 referred to the owner
=====
## Owner instruction 2026-11-16 — the medical taxonomy, the medical maps and the medical codes are deleted

**Owner's words, quoted (typed):**

> "delete medical taxonomy , medical maps and medical codes btw"

and, in the same session, on how the work is to be carried out (a process instruction, not a ruling on the lens):

> "perform carefully thoroughly stacking all items into one batch for pr then running close sequence on that"

**Readings.** [ASSUMPTION: "medical taxonomy" is the table `base_taxonomy_medical`; "medical maps" are `identity_medical_map` and `icf_medical_map`; "medical codes" are the `medical_code` column of every table that carried one (`gaps`, `specifications`, `search_executions`, `extraction_lens_links`, `determination_gates`, `source_value_extractions`) and the `MD-` code vocabulary — basis: the statement names the three things in the order the schema holds them, and no other object in the schema is called medical.] [ASSUMPTION: "delete" means the schema objects, the writer (`db.py add-medical`, `insert_medical`), every `--medical` flag, the check `medical_lens_integrity` and the contract criteria that read it, and the prose that offers the lens; it does not mean editing frozen records (ledger entries, `decisions/`, `sessions/`, committed migrations), which stay as the record of what was ruled when — basis: rule 0 of CLAUDE.md and `decisions/DR-2026-09-26-recurring-defect-shapes-remediation.md` on in-place edits.] [ASSUMPTION: the word "medical" in the `domain` of a term (`terms.domain`, `dbcore.NON_QUANTITY_DOMAINS`) names a kind of concept a parameter may not be, not the lens, and stays — basis: it is a vocabulary of terms, read by T-010's refusal, and no row of the deleted tables is involved.] [ASSUMPTION: the lens set becomes three, identity, ICF and access need, and the "at least one" rule of D-0182 reads over those three — basis: nothing in the statement adds a lens in its place.] No row was lost: every deleted table held no row and every deleted column was NULL on every row (measured before the migration was applied: the three tables held 0 rows, and `COUNT(medical_code)` was 0 on each of the six tables).

**What it supersedes, on contact (rule 0).** None of these is edited; this entry is the record, as `Supersession record 2026-11-15 — three March 2026 rules overtaken, recorded by this entry (T-001)` records for a ledger target, and for the same reason (a `SUPERSEDES` pair cannot name a target in this ledger, and `decisions/` is not edited in place).
1. The medical lens of `decisions/DR-2026-08-27-four-taxonomies-are-browsing-lenses.md` (D-0170: "we give our users the choice of what model they want to use to browse the site"), as to the medical taxonomy only; the identity, ICF and access-need lenses stand.
2. `decisions/DR-2026-09-11-adjudication-delegated-medical-lens-enforced.md` and the ledger entries "Owner ruling 2026-09-11 — adjudication delegated for a named set; the medical lens gets filled", "Owner ruling 2026-09-11 — ICD-11 is the medical-lens source, at BLOCK grain, for correspondence", "The medical lens is DEMAND-POPULATED, not pre-populated — the owner's granularity doubt, measured" and its "CORRECTION, same day".
3. The answer to OD-15 (the medical lens and the WHO licence), in "Owner answers 2026-11-12 — OD-04 (research scope), OD-23 …", which is moot with the lens.
4. The count of four in the 2026-08-28 ruling ("four lens columns") and in D-0182's "at least one" (now of three); the clause that `population_code` is retired in favour of "the four".
5. Remediation-plan tasks that exist for the medical lens (T-077, T-103) and the clauses of other task files that name it: each is amended in the pull request that carries this entry.

**What it does not decide.** Whether a diagnosis may be recorded anywhere else (a term, an observed phrase, a note): it may, as the evidence states it; nothing in the schema keys on it. Whether the ICD-11 anchoring work already in the retrieval log is kept: it is a record and stays. The migration is `scripts/migrations/138_drop_medical_lens.sql`; the rule version of the determination engine moved to `pilot-7` because the derivation hash had a slot for the fourth lens (`test_db_integrity` K01 keeps `pilot-6` on the four-slot form).

CONDITION: any session meeting `medical_code`, `base_taxonomy_medical`, `identity_medical_map`, `icf_medical_map`, `add-medical`, `--medical`, `MD-` codes, "the fourth lens", "four lens columns" or "the medical lens" outside a frozen record.
ACTION: (1) Treat the lens as deleted: do not restore it, fill it or key a cell on it. (2) A phrase in a frozen record that offers it is history, not a gap. (3) A restatement outside the ledger that still names it is repaired where it stands. (4) The medical model as a *framing to avoid* (`voice-style`, `framing-checker`, the social-model posture of the mission) is doctrine and is untouched.
DATE: 2026-11-16 — owner instruction (typed words, quoted above).

## Correction 2026-11-16 — to the entry that deletes the medical lens: two earlier acceptances lose their premise (the `SCI` edge, OI-48), and one question the instruction does not answer

Found by the read-only critic of the commit that carried the deletion, by searching the ledger for the medical lens in ACTION and answer lines rather than in titles. The entry "Owner instruction 2026-11-16 — the medical taxonomy, the medical maps and the medical codes are deleted" is not edited; it listed five things it supersedes and missed these.

1. **"Owner clarification 2026-11-12 (seventh set) — SCI is basically WHEEL and LMB is basically PROSTH"**, ACTION (4): "Keep impairment level in the medical lens and ICF codes." Superseded as to the medical lens; the clause now reads "keep impairment level in ICF codes", where an ICF body-function code holds the function an injury changes and not the injury.
2. **"Owner answers 2026-11-13 (tenth set) …", OI-48 — the `SCI` edge**, selected "Accept": "the injury and its level are held in the medical lens and ICF b-codes; `SCI` has no identity code of its own." The owner accepted that `SCI` loses its identity code **on that premise**. Half of the premise no longer exists. `SCI` is still active in `base_taxonomy_identity`, and no task has retired it (T-102 has not run).

**The question this puts to the owner, not decided here:** with the medical lens gone, where is a spinal cord injury and its level held for a group the project serves, and is `SCI` still retired into `WHEEL` (the OI-48 answer) or kept as an identity code that the wheelchair-user code does not replace? [ASSUMPTION: T-102 must not retire `SCI` until the owner answers — basis: the acceptance was given on a premise the owner has since removed, and a retirement is not undone by the sanctioned verbs (`retire-identity` refuses a code that is another code's successor).] It is registered as OI-77 in `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md` and named in `tasks/T-102-design.md` and `tasks/T-102-mobility-split.md` as a stop.

**A second question the instruction leaves open:** eight live `terms` carry `domain = 'medical'` (search vocabulary: conditions and diagnoses a source names). They are not a lens and no cell is keyed on them, so they were kept. Whether "medical codes" reaches them is the owner's reading, not a fact.

**CLAUDE.md rule 5.** Its sentence "A column a committed data migration INSERTs can never be dropped" was true of a drop the replay plan orders before those data migrations, and false of one it orders after them. Migration 138 drops `medical_code`, which many committed data migrations name, and the rebuild reproduces the database because `migrate_db.build_plan()` replays them first. The sentence is corrected in the same pull request to say that.

CONDITION: any session meeting the `SCI` edge, OI-48, the seventh-set ACTION (4), or a task that places an impairment level in a lens.
ACTION: (1) Read both clauses above as superseded as to the medical lens. (2) Do not run T-102's retirement of `SCI` before the owner answers OI-77. (3) Do not key a determination on a diagnosis term.
DATE: 2026-11-16 — correction by the recorder; the questions are the owner's.

## Owner answers 2026-11-17 — OD-68 (one written word naming different concepts in two languages), OD-69 (what "category" means) and OD-70 (who assigns the evidence tier)

Written by the coordinator after an Opus design of the mapping between codes and identities (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/MAPPING-DESIGN.md`) was attacked by an independent critic and revised. **Not the owner's words.** It corrects two readings recorded earlier in this ledger, on contact (CLAUDE.md rule 0), and registers one question.

**[CORRECTION: the ACTION of the entry 'populations are still coded, through the ICF and access-need lenses' (2026-11-14, sixteenth set, last) says to "reach the populations through the mapping" and not to "store the derived identity beside them". That was the recorder's reading, marked [ASSUMPTION] in that entry, and not the owner's words ("ICF and access needs are supposed to be mapped to populations too so populations still get coded as a result"). It is replaced by: the recording session judges and writes the identity link of a code value, with its basis `context` and its warrant, in the same call as the ICF and access-need links ("at the moment of recording the row is when you will have best idea of context"; "use contextual judgment"); the maps (`identity_icf_map`, and the b/d rows of `access_need_icf`) are the writer's source of proposals, shown with their mapping confidence and provenance, never a lookup the engine consults at read time.]** The critic's evidence for the correction: a read-time crossing intersecting an ICF and a need link reached no group at all for the owner's own mounting-height default, ten identities have no ICF map row, and the live figure 166 (rollator walking, one d450 link) would reach five groups; and the lens table already allows several lens rows per figure (extractions 33 and 165 carry an identity row beside a need row), so writing the identity breaks no check.

Prose supersession only: the ledger cannot carry a marker beside its own earlier text.

**What this does not change.** D-0184 and OR-1 stand: a figure reaches a determination only through the lens tags written on it; the engine is not edited; no supersession of OR-1 is made.

- **OD-67: may the batch's full list of new population-to-ICF rows be confirmed in one answer?** The batch (the research task that mints the ICF codes d4452, d4153, d4154, titles d415, and writes the rows that map wheelchair users to reaching and to a seated or standing posture, and the five groups with no ICF row, ADHD, DeafBlind, epilepsy, MS and vestibular, re-derived from the retired axis map) judges each row; because these rows decide which groups are proposed for every code value, they are population taxonomy and the owner's (OD-47 referral; the mobility crossings went to the owner as OI-03). # CLAUDE.md — working guide for the Accessible Built Environments Guidebook

## Goal

The owner's goal, verbatim (2026-11-20): *"we research, we record, we verify we recorded things accurately, we
evaluate things in context with other related things, we synthesize then show"*.

**The project is simple** (owner, 2026-11-25: *"this is a simple project where we build as little machinery as possible to enact our goal"*; also *"Remember that this project is simple!!!"*). Meet the goal with the least machinery: §8's order applies to every task, and a table, verb, check or rule that the goal does not need is not built.

The project is a database that records research properly, and a pipeline that processes it; `base` is the owner's
request layer, standing where the owner would otherwise ask for a topic directly. The owner reads only English, so
three things are never to be got wrong:

1. **Fetch before you write any author, title or figure.** A bibliographic field is never written from memory.
2. **Keep the original beside every translated figure,** and show an English rendering that records who translated
   and who reviewed it, and when (`translations`; `db.py translations --show` prints each reviewed one beside its
   original); never English into `claimed_value` or `claimed_unit`.
3. **Co-1 co-producers are evidence and stay credited.**

This file holds **process, workflow and rules only**; every volatile fact (counts, versions, CI state) is derived,
never stated. Where it disagrees with `decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md`, that
instrument wins and this file is what to correct — **unless a live owner ruling has superseded the instrument itself,
per rule 0, in which case the ruling wins over both.**

**Correction histories do not live here.** When a sentence in this file is found wrong, fix the
sentence and put the account of the error in the commit message; `git log -p CLAUDE.md` is the record.
This file is loaded into every turn, so every line of narrative is paid for on every turn.

---

Each rule carries what enforces it. **"NOT ENFORCED" means you are the gate** — no check will catch
you, and the unenforced rules are where the defects recorded below actually occurred.

**0. A live owner statement supersedes every prior ratified record it touches, on contact.** Record
the supersession; never weigh the ruling against the paperwork it changes. A DR, a RULE, an ADOPTED
directive are what a ruling *changes* — never an argument against it. Numbered 0 because the rest of
this file tilts the other way.
*Proof: on 2026-08-18 the owner ruled `axes` a bad coined term, marked "do not relitigate", and the
next day a batch framed four of five searches on bare `axis_code`, hiding a second mechanism.*
→ **PARTLY ENFORCED** by `supersession_backpointer_audit`, for supersessions a `SUPERSEDES` line
names. Naming them is yours.

**1. Commit format.** `{skill-name}: {action} [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM]`, timestamp last, from
`date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'`. Use `governance` when no project skill fits.
→ Enforced by `check_commit_msg.py`, **push events only** (`ci.yml:257`) — skipped on every PR.
## 9. What this project is

A reference on architecture, accessibility and built-environment standards centred on **disabled
people**. Fixed doctrine: a **thinking tool and advocacy project, not an authority** — *"the purpose
of this guidebook is to get people to ask the right questions."* Not a prescription manual, not a
legal authority, not a substitute for professional judgment. "Inclusive / accessible / universal"
here always means *inclusion of persons with disabilities*.

Pre-launch, single author (`@jordanelias`). The governance and tooling are elaborate; **the content
is barely started.** Query the DB for the real state.

| What to do now | `decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md` |

## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (fourteenth) — advocacy groups and disability ethics are the lens for grouping, sorting and taxonomy

Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), while a research pass on whether "mobility" and other population umbrellas make sense as identity categories was running, recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "use advocacy groups and disability ethics as a lens for grouping/sorting/taxonomy"

**What this records.** How disabled people organise themselves through their own advocacy groups, and what disability ethics proposes, are to be the lens through which the project groups, sorts and classifies people. It is stated as a method for the analysis of the taxonomy and says nothing yet about which categories result.

**What it does not decide.** Which advocacy groups count, how their categories are turned into codes, how the ethical approaches are weighed where they disagree, and which of the registry's present identity codes change. The population taxonomy remains the owner's. It does not supersede the 2026-08-28 ruling that a determination is keyed on four lens columns, nor the project's rule to work from the ICF and access-need frame; it is a lens on how the groupings within them are drawn. [ASSUMPTION: "advocacy groups" is read as disabled people's own organisations and self-advocacy groups (the CRPD's "representative organizations"), not charities or bodies speaking for disabled people; unratified.]

CONDITION: any session defining, splitting, merging, renaming or sorting identity or population categories.
ACTION: (1) Take the organisation of disabled people's own advocacy groups, and the approaches of disability ethics, as the lens for how categories are drawn. (2) Record the group or ethical source a grouping rests on, as provenance. (3) Leave the choice among competing groupings to the owner. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.
DATE: 2026-11-12 — owner statement, quoted above.

governance: write the supersession pointer when a retired cell is re-determined [2026-11-15 19:03]

T-011. Before: re-determining a cell (retire, then run the engine again) left the
retired row's superseded_by_specification_id NULL, so nothing linked the old value
to the one that replaced it. On a copy of the live database, parameter 3 x MOB: the
newest row was live and the row before it was retired with a NULL pointer. After:
the engine, in the same transaction and in the emitted SQL, points the most
recently retired row of the cell that holds no pointer at the new determination
(8 -> 9, then after a second retirement 9 -> 10, the first link untouched). Older
retired rows with no pointer are not back-filled; they are named on stderr.

One writer of the column: dbcore.SUPERSEDE_SQL is the UPDATE, used by
db.py retire-specification --superseded-by and by the engine. The cell predicate
the already-determined refusal used is now dbcore-free module text in assess_cell
(CELL_WHERE, _cell_vals), read by that refusal and by the link, so the two cannot
disagree on blank-versus-NULL. The refusal's own sentence ("the new determination
